thread:
alex: Found a public gist that contains a KMS-wrapped ciphertext blob and an SA email. Not the private key, but enough context to worry about possible replay/unwrapping. tagging #eng-security for triage

maria: don't click anything more. paste the gist id here and the raw snippet if you grabbed it. also did you download it or just saw it via google cache?

alex: gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/abC1d2e3
snippet:
```
wrapped: CiQAZ...base64...
metadata: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/shortname/cryptoKeys/transactions/cryptoKeyVersions/1
sa: redwood-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

vault-bot: New leak ticket created: SEC-2026-318 — priority: high — assigned: unassigned

jun: what project is that SA attached to? if it's a service account key material leak we should revoke the key immediately and rotate the KMS key version. also start IAM audit to see if the SA was used to impersonate anything.

tara: oncall here — I can revoke the exposed SA key now. steps: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=redwood-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` then `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=...` we'll also remove any user-managed keys bound to that SA.

alex: revoked the key (deleted KEY_ID abcdef123). Not sure if there are copies elsewhere. I also saved the original gist text to SEC-2026-318 evidence folder.

maria: if that ciphertext came from Vault transit, we need to rotate the transit key and rewrap stored ciphertexts. I'll check Vault audit logs for any decrypts referencing that ciphertext. Also will lock down the transit key ACLs to a single rewrap SA.

ben: propose a short-lived RBAC change: create role `kms-emergency-unwrap` scoped to `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/shortname` with only `locations/global/keyRings/shortname/cryptoKeys/cryptoKeyVersions/cryptoKeyVersionId/restore` (or closest minimal perms) and grant to responders for 2 hours. We'll audit the bindings afterwards. cc @legal on disclosure needs.

jun: I'll handle KMS rotation. plan: create new key version, mark old version disabled, run rewrap tool to migrate ciphertexts. command: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=shortname --location=global --keyring=shortname` then run `python tools/rewrap.py --src=projects/.../cryptoKeys/.../versions/1 --dst=.../versions/3` in a controlled batch.

alex: quick wins checklist (initial containment):
1) revoke exposed SA key (done)
2) rotate KMS key version (jun)
3) run Vault rewrap of transit ciphertexts (maria)
4) repo/partner scrub for gist content & delete mirrors (ben)
5) update audit stream to SIEM and preserve logs (tara)
ETA: 2h for containment baseline.

maria: I'll own Vault rewrap + metadata update. I'll also add an audit webhook for any decrypt calls to the transit mount. drafting notice for partners and support.

oncall-bot: Incident SEC-2026-318 assigned to alex, jun, maria, tara, ben. Pager duty notified.

jun: rotated KMS key in `redwood-prod-kms` -> created version 3. Dry-run of rewrap worked on staging. Running production rewrap in 10m.

alex: rewrap dry-run logs look good. pushing to prod after 15m, will watch for decryption errors. notifying product owners of short maintenance window.

maria: rewrap finished, updated Vault ciphertext metadata to point to new key version. Post-rotation audit shows no unexpected decrypt calls in the last 30m. Found two matches in an archived partner repo during creds-scan; flagged for deletion and partner notified.

ben: added forward of KMS & Vault audit logs to SIEM index `sec-audit-rotations` with 2y retention. also created ad-hoc RBAC review board meeting tomorrow 10:00 to tighten key bindings and remove broad roles.

tara: postmortem action: add pre-commit hook to block private keys/SA JSONs and update onboarding checklist to include `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list` hygiene. I'll open a PR for the infra docs.

alex: containment closed for now. I'll open the full incident ticket with timeline and assign postmortem owners. great job all. :tada:
